extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community — investigators, applicants, institutional research administrators, and grant staff
extracted.subtask_description: A news/updates digest about NIH extramural policies, processes, and resources that affect grant applications, review, data sharing, and research practices. Intended to inform investigators and institutional staff about changes and new guidance to incorporate into proposals and administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting appropriate models (New Approach Methodologies - NAMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches to advance understanding of human health and disease; investigators should select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages choosing models that enhance human relevance and translational potential; the emphasis is on scientific appropriateness to the research question rather than favoring any single model class.

rubrics_metrics.name: PF5 Collaborative International Research Projects application format and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Watch NIH’s 6-minute overview of the new Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) award structure to learn key features, application format, and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should follow the PF5-specific application format and be aware that award splitting into linked awards can occur after review and prior to Just-in-Time — plan proposals and budgets accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: A new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format is available based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing DMS plans, use the 2026 pilot format and include the specified required elements; the new format simplifies expectations — consult the resource for the exact elements to include.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replication and reproducibility expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan advances a commitment to replication and reproducibility and has launched a Replication and Reproducibility Initiative to drive, incentivize and institutionalize replication and reproducibility efforts across the biomedical research enterprise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications, awards, and institutional practices should embed replication and reproducibility considerations; applicants may be expected to address these topics where relevant and consider replication-focused designs or plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of 'Competitive But Not Discussed' (triage/score interpretation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Following emergency modifications to review processes, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as 'competitive but not discussed' — recognizing that strong applications may fall below a 33% cut-off.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants receiving this designation should understand it reflects review triage practices (not necessarily poor quality); investigate reviewer summary statements and next steps (e.g., Just-in-Time) for responses or opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralization of NIH peer review within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH announced that all peer review would be centralized within CSR; the consolidation aims to strengthen efficiency, competition, and transparency in peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and institutions should be aware that peer review workflows, study section assignments, and possibly review expectations may be affected by centralization; monitor CSR guidance for any procedural or format changes that affect submissions.
